hypothesis: The prior momentum portfolio's consistently negative Sharpe indicates that cross-sectional momentum is the wrong sign in this universe/period. I will flip it into a low-turnover cross-sectional reversal strategy: rank stocks by market-relative 20-, 60-, and 120-day returns, go long the relative losers and short the relative winners, size positions inversely to realized volatility, and rebalance only monthly using the prior month-end signal to keep turnover and transaction costs low. Dollar-neutrality and per-name caps are enforced; the hypothesis is that reversing the sign of the trend signal, residualizing against the equal-weighted market, and avoiding daily churn will improve risk-adjusted returns relative to the failed momentum version.
